nodes.name: Proof of Lemma D.2
nodes.statement:
First, fix $n$ large enough, such that the bound of Condition~ef{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:Huber} holds, the pseudo parameter of Lemma~ef{lemma:pseudo} exists and the bound of Lemma~ef{lemma:pseudoBound} applies. Fix $\mathbb M\in\mathsf{M}_n$ and ${\mathbb P}_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(	au)$. Since $H_{\mathbb M,n}(y, eta) =$ \linebreak $X_n[M]'D_{\mathbb M,n}(y, eta)X_n[M]$, for a diagonal matrix $D_{\mathbb M,n}(y, eta)$ whose $i$-th diagonal entry is given by $$ -y_i\ddot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M] eta) - (1-y_i)\ddot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M] eta)\;>\;0, $$ in view of Conditions~ef{cond:H}(ef{cH:cdf},ef{cH:concave},ef{cH:C2}), we see that $H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)$ is positive definite. Moreover, from continuity and positivity of $-\ddot{\phi}_j$, $j=1,2$, Lemma~ef{lemma:pseudoBound} and finiteness of $\mathcal H$, we conclude that the diagonal entries of $D_{\mathbb M,n}(y, eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*({\mathbb P}_n))$ are lower and upper bounded by positive constants that depend only on $	au$ and $C$. This finishes the claim in ef{l:Hcont:A}. Consider now  egin{align} &\sup_{ eta\in N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)} \|H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} H_{\mathbb M,n}(y, eta) H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| 
otag\ &\quad\le\; \|X_n[M]H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}\|^2 \sup_{ eta\in N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)} \|D_{\mathbb M,n}(y, eta) - D_{\mathbb M,n}(y, eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*({\mathbb P}_n)\| 
otag\ &\quad\le\;  rac{\|X_n[M](X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{-1}X_n[M]'\|}{\min_{i=1,\dots, n}(-y_i\ddot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) - (1-y_i)\ddot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*))} 	imes
otag\ &\quad\quad\quad \sup_{ eta\in N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)}\max_{\substack{i=1,\dots, n\j=1,2}} |\ddot \phi_j(X_{i,n}[M] eta) - \ddot \phi_j(X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)|. \end{align} We have just seen that the minimum on the far right side of the previous display is lower bounded by a positive constant that depends only on $	au$ and $C$. To finish the proof, note that for $ eta\in N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)$, we have  egin{align*} &|X_{i,n}[M] eta - X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*| \ &\le \|X_{i,n}[M](X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{-1/2}\| \|(X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{1/2}( eta -  eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)\|\le \delta \sqrt{C/n} \end{align*} and that $|X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*|\le K^*(	au,C)$, by Lemma~ef{lemma:pseudoBound}. Therefore, by uniform continuity of $\ddot{\phi}_j$ on the compact interval $[-K^*(	au,C) - \delta \sqrt{C}, K^*(	au,C) + \delta \sqrt{C}]$, for every $\eta>0$, there exists $n_0 = n_0(\eta, 	au, \delta, C,h)$, such that the supremum in \eqref{eq:Hcontinuity} is bounded by $\eta$, for all $n\ge n_0$. Since $\mathcal H$ is finite, the proof of ef{l:Hcont:B} is finished. For part~ef{l:Hcont:C}, simply combine part~ef{l:Hcont:A} and Condition~ef{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:eigen}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the diagonal weights using Lemma D.1; continuity of the Hessian by uniform continuity of $\ddot\phi_j$ on a compact interval.

otag\ &\quad\le\;  rac{\|X_n[M](X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{-1}X_n[M]'\|}{\min_{i=1,\dots, n}(-y_i\ddot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) - (1-y_i)\ddot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*))} 	imes
otag\ &\quad\quad\quad \sup_{ eta\in N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)}\max_{\substack{i=1,\dots, n\j=1,2}} |\ddot \phi_j(X_{i,n}[M] eta) - \ddot \phi_j(X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)|. \end{align} We have just seen that the minimum on the far right side of the previous display is lower bounded by a positive constant that depends only on $	au$ and $C$. To finish the proof, note that for $ eta\in N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)$, we have  egin{align*} &|X_{i,n}[M] eta - X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*| \ &\le \|X_{i,n}[M](X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{-1/2}\| \|(X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{1/2}( eta -  eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)\|\le \delta \sqrt{C/n} \end{align*} and that $|X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*|\le K^*(	au,C)$, by Lemma~ef{lemma:pseudoBound}. Therefore, by uniform continuity of $\ddot{\phi}_j$ on the compact interval $[-K^*(	au,C) - \delta \sqrt{C}, K^*(	au,C) + \delta \sqrt{C}]$, for every $\eta>0$, there exists $n_0 = n_0(\eta, 	au, \delta, C,h)$, such that the supremum in \eqref{eq:Hcontinuity} is bounded by $\eta$, for all $n\ge n_0$. Since $\mathcal H$ is finite, the proof of ef{l:Hcont:B} is finished.
nodes.statement_short: Part (ii): uniform continuity of $\ddot\phi_j$ on a compact interval.

nodes.name: Equation (D.22) [eq:Hcontinuity]
nodes.statement:
&\sup_{ eta\in N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)} \|H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} H_{\mathbb M,n}(y, eta) H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| 
otag\ &\quad\le\; \|X_n[M]H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}\|^2 \sup_{ eta\in N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)} \|D_{\mathbb M,n}(y, eta) - D_{\mathbb M,n}(y, eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*({\mathbb P}_n)\| 
otag\ &\quad\le\;  rac{\|X_n[M](X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{-1}X_n[M]'\|}{\min_{i=1,\dots, n}(-y_i\ddot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) - (1-y_i)\ddot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*))} 	imes
otag\ &\quad\quad\quad \sup_{ eta\in N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)}\max_{\substack{i=1,\dots, n\j=1,2}} |\ddot \phi_j(X_{i,n}[M] eta) - \ddot \phi_j(X_{i,n}[M] eta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)|.
nodes.label: eq:Hcontinuity

nodes.name: Part (iii)
nodes.statement: For part~\ref{l:Hcont:C}, simply combine part~\ref{l:Hcont:A} and Condition~\ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:eigen}.
nodes.statement_short: Part (iii) from part (i) and the eigenvalue condition.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.10
nodes.statement_short: Taylor-expand the log-likelihood and show it decreases on the boundary of a shrinking neighbourhood with high probability. Key step: Markov bound on the score plus Hessian continuity (Lemma D.2).

nodes.name: Pointer
nodes.statement: The proof is a variation of the consistency part of the proof of Theorem~4 in \citet{Fahrmeir90}.
nodes.statement_short: Follows Fahrmeir and Kaufmann's consistency argument.

nodes.name: Expansion
nodes.statement: Fix $n$ large enough, such that the bound of Condition~\ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:Huber} holds, the pseudo parameter of Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudo} exists and the bound of Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudoBound} applies. Fix $\mathbb M\in\mathsf{M}_n$ and ${\mathbb P}_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)$, write $\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^* = \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*({\mathbb P}_n)$ and note that by Condition~\ref{cond:H}\eqref{cH:C2}, the function $\beta\mapsto \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)$ is twice continuously differentiable on ${\mathbb R}^{m(\mathbb M)}$ and thus, for every $y\in\{0,1\}^n$, admits the expansion \begin{align*} \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta) \quad&=\quad \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) \;+\; (\beta-\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)'U_{M,n}^{1/2}U_{M,n}^{-1/2}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) \\ &\quad-\; \frac{1}{2}(\beta-\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)'U_{M,n}^{1/2}U_{M,n}^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\tilde{\beta}_n)U_{M,n}^{-1/2}U_{M,n}^{1/2}(\beta-\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*), \end{align*} for some $\tilde{\beta}_n\in\{a\beta + (1-a)\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^* : a\in[0,1]\}$, and where $s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) = \frac{\partial \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)}{\partial \beta}\Big|_{\beta=\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*}$, $H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta) = -\frac{\partial \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)}{\partial\beta\partial\beta'}$, and $U_{M,n} = X_n[M]'X_n[M]/n$.
nodes.statement_short: Second-order Taylor expansion of the log-likelihood.

nodes.name: Rescaling
nodes.statement: For $\delta>0$, define $\lambda_n = \sqrt{n}U_{M,n}^{1/2}(\beta-\beta_{\mathbb M.n}^*)/\delta$ to rewrite the previous equation as \begin{align*} \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta) \;-\; \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) \;&=\; \delta \lambda_n'U_{M,n}^{-1/2}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)/\sqrt{n} \\ &\quad-\; \frac{1}{2}\delta^2 \lambda_n'U_{M,n}^{-1/2}(H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\tilde{\beta}_n)/n)U_{M,n}^{-1/2}\lambda_n, \end{align*} for all $\beta\in{\mathbb R}^{m(\mathbb M)}$ and all $y\in\{0,1\}^n$.
nodes.statement_short: Rescale with $\lambda_n$.

nodes.name: Boundary bound
nodes.statement: For $N_n(\delta) := N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)$ as in Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:B}, define $ L_n(y,\delta) := \inf_{\beta\in N_n(\delta)} \lambda_{\min}\left(U_{M,n}^{-1/2}(H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)/n)U_{M,n}^{-1/2}\right), $ take $\beta\in\partial N_n(\delta) = \{\beta\in{\mathbb R}^{m(\mathbb M)} : \|\sqrt{n}U_{M,n}^{1/2}(\beta-\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)\|= \delta\}$ and observe that now $\|\lambda_n\|=1$, $\delta\lambda_n'U_{M,n}^{-1/2}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)/\sqrt{n} \le \delta \|U_{M,n}^{-1/2}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)/\sqrt{n}\|$ and \begin{align*} \frac{1}{2}\delta^2 L_n(y,\delta) \;&\le\; \frac{1}{2}\delta^2 \lambda_{\min}\left(U_{M,n}^{-1/2}(H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\tilde{\beta})/n)U_{M,n}^{-1/2}\right) \\ \;&\le\; \frac{1}{2}\delta^2 \lambda_n'U_{M,n}^{-1/2}(H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\tilde{\beta})/n)U_{M,n}^{-1/2}\lambda_n, \end{align*} for all $y\in\{0,1\}^n$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound the quadratic term on the boundary by $L_n$.

nodes.name: Existence of local maximum
nodes.statement: Therefore, we have the inclusion \begin{align*} E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta) &:= \{y\in\{0,1\}^n:\delta\|U_{M,n}^{-1/2}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)/\sqrt{n}\| < \delta^2 L_n(y,\delta)/2\} \\ &\subseteq \{y\in\{0,1\}^n : \forall \beta\in\partial N_n(\delta) : \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta) < \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)\} =: F_n(\delta). \end{align*} As a consequence, for every $y \in E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)$, the function $\beta\mapsto \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)$ has a local maximum $\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)$ on the interior of $N_n(\delta)$. By strict concavity (Conditions~\ref{cond:H}\eqref{cH:concave} and \ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:rank}), this is a unique global maximum.
nodes.statement_short: On $E(\delta)$ the likelihood decreases on the boundary, giving a unique interior maximum.

nodes.name: Deviation bound
nodes.statement: Moreover, we have $F_n(\delta) \subseteq \{y: \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) \in N_n(\delta)\} = \{y: \|\sqrt{n}U_{M,n}^{1/2}(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)\| \le \delta\}$. Hence, $$ {\mathbb P}_n(\|\sqrt{n}U_{M,n}^{1/2}(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)\| > \delta) \;\le\; {\mathbb P}_n(E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)^c). $$
nodes.statement_short: Deviation probability bounded by $P(E(\delta)^c)$.

nodes.name: Remaining
nodes.statement: It remains to verify that ${\mathbb P}_n(E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)^c)$ is small for large $n$, uniformly in $\mathbb M$ and ${\mathbb P}_n$.
nodes.statement_short: Remains to bound $P(E^c)$ uniformly.

nodes.name: Markov bound
nodes.statement:
Take $\varepsilon>0$ and note that  egin{align} {\mathbb P}_n(E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)^c) \;&\le\; 
otag {\mathbb P}_n(4\|U_{M,n}^{-1/2}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(\cdot)/\sqrt{n}\|^2\ge \delta^2 L_n^2(\cdot,\delta), L_n^2(\cdot,\delta) \ge \varepsilon^2 ) 
otag\ &\;\quad\;+\; {\mathbb P}_n(L_n^2(\cdot,\delta) < \varepsilon^2 ) \ &\le \; {\mathbb P}_n(4\|U_{M,n}^{-1/2}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(\cdot)/\sqrt{n}\|^2\ge \delta^2 \varepsilon^2) \;+\; {\mathbb P}_n(L_n^2(\cdot,\delta) < \varepsilon^2 )
otag\ &\le \; 4 rac{\mathrm{trace}(U_{M,n}^{-1/2}{\mathbb{V}}_n(s_{\mathbb M,n}^*/\sqrt{n})U_{M,n}^{-1/2})}{\delta^2\varepsilon^2} \;+\; {\mathbb P}_n(L_n(\cdot,\delta) < \varepsilon ), 
otag \end{align} in view of Markov's inequality and since ${\mathbb E}_n[s_{\mathbb M,n}^*] = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Markov bound on the score norm plus $P(L_n<\varepsilon)$.

nodes.name: Equation (D.23) [eq:lUnifCons:trace]
nodes.statement:
{\mathbb P}_n(E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)^c) \;&\le\; 
otag {\mathbb P}_n(4\|U_{M,n}^{-1/2}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(\cdot)/\sqrt{n}\|^2\ge \delta^2 L_n^2(\cdot,\delta), L_n^2(\cdot,\delta) \ge \varepsilon^2 ) 
otag\ &\;\quad\;+\; {\mathbb P}_n(L_n^2(\cdot,\delta) < \varepsilon^2 ) \ &\le \; {\mathbb P}_n(4\|U_{M,n}^{-1/2}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(\cdot)/\sqrt{n}\|^2\ge \delta^2 \varepsilon^2) \;+\; {\mathbb P}_n(L_n^2(\cdot,\delta) < \varepsilon^2 )
otag\ &\le \; 4 rac{\mathrm{trace}(U_{M,n}^{-1/2}{\mathbb{V}}_n(s_{\mathbb M,n}^*/\sqrt{n})U_{M,n}^{-1/2})}{\delta^2\varepsilon^2} \;+\; {\mathbb P}_n(L_n(\cdot,\delta) < \varepsilon ), 
otag
nodes.label: eq:lUnifCons:trace

nodes.name: Score variance
nodes.statement: Note that ${\mathbb{V}}_n(s_{\mathbb M,n}^*) = X_n[M]'V_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}^*X_n[M]$, for a diagonal matrix $V_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}^*$ whose diagonal entries satisfy \begin{align*} [V_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}^*]_{ii} \;&=\; {\mathbb P}_{i,n}(\{1\}){\mathbb P}_{i,n}(\{0\})(\dot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) - \dot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*))^2 \\ \;&\le\; \sup_{|\gamma|\le K^*(\tau,C)}(\dot{\phi}_1(\gamma) - \dot{\phi}_2(\gamma))^2, \end{align*} for the constant $K^*(\tau,C)$ of Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudoBound}. Thus, the trace on the last line of display~\eqref{eq:lUnifCons:trace} is bounded by $p\max_{h\in\mathcal H}\sup_{|\gamma|\le K^*(\tau,C)}(\dot{\phi}_1(\gamma) - \dot{\phi}_2(\gamma))^2$, which does not depend on $n$, $\mathbb M$ or ${\mathbb P}_n$.
nodes.statement_short: Score variance bounded uniformly via Lemma D.1.

nodes.name: Hessian term
nodes.statement: Finally, to bound the remaining probability, note that $L_n(y,\delta)$ is lower bounded by the product of $\lambda_{\min}(U_{M,n}^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)U_{M,n}^{-1/2})/n$ and $\inf_{\beta\in N_n(\delta)} \lambda_{\min}(H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2})$. The first factor is itself lower bounded by the positive constant $\underline{K}(\tau, C)$ from Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:A}. Thus, ${\mathbb P}_n(L_n(\cdot,\delta) < \varepsilon )$ is upper bounded by $$ {\mathbb P}_n\left( \sup_{\beta\in N_{n}(\delta)} \left\| H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)} \right\| > 1- \frac{\varepsilon}{\underline{K}(\tau, C)} \right). $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound $P(L_n<\varepsilon)$ via Hessian continuity.

nodes.name: Uniform bound
nodes.statement: Choosing $\varepsilon = \underline{K}(\tau, C)/2$ and using Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:B}, we conclude that for every $\delta>0$, \begin{align} &\sup_{\mathbb M\in\mathsf{M}_n}\sup_{{\mathbb P}_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)} {\mathbb P}_n\left( \left\| (X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{1/2}(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n} - \beta^*_{\mathbb M,n}({\mathbb P}_n))\right\| > \delta\right) \\ &\quad\le \sup_{\mathbb M\in\mathsf{M}_n}\sup_{{\mathbb P}_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)} {\mathbb P}_n(E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)^c)\\ &\quad\le 16\frac{p\max_{h\in\mathcal H}\sup_{|\gamma|\le K^*(\tau,C)}(\dot{\phi}_1(\gamma) - \dot{\phi}_2(\gamma))^2}{\delta^2\underline{K}(\tau,C)^2} + o(1), \end{align} where the $o(1)$ term refers to convergence as $n\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma D.2 gives the uniform bound.

nodes.name: Equation (D.24) [eq:lUnifCons:sup]
nodes.statement: &\sup_{\mathbb M\in\mathsf{M}_n}\sup_{{\mathbb P}_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)} {\mathbb P}_n\left( \left\| (X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{1/2}(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n} - \beta^*_{\mathbb M,n}({\mathbb P}_n))\right\| > \delta\right) \\ &\quad\le \sup_{\mathbb M\in\mathsf{M}_n}\sup_{{\mathbb P}_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)} {\mathbb P}_n(E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)^c)\\ &\quad\le 16\frac{p\max_{h\in\mathcal H}\sup_{|\gamma|\le K^*(\tau,C)}(\dot{\phi}_1(\gamma) - \dot{\phi}_2(\gamma))^2}{\delta^2\underline{K}(\tau,C)^2} + o(1),
nodes.label: eq:lUnifCons:sup

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Now, to establish the asymptotic existence of the MLE, we simply take $E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n} :=E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta_n)$, for $\delta_n\to\infty$ sufficiently slowly as $n\to\infty$. For the uniform consistency part, note that the limit superior as $n\to\infty$ of the expression in \eqref{eq:lUnifCons:sup} is bounded by a quantity that converges to zero as $\delta\to\infty$. \hfill{\qed}
nodes.statement_short: Let $\delta_n\to\infty$ slowly for existence; let $\delta\to\infty$ for consistency.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.11
nodes.statement: Fix $n\in{\mathbb N}$, a candidate model $\mathbb M\in\mathsf{M}_n$ and ${\mathbb P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)$, and let ${\mathbb E}_n$ and ${\mathbb V}_n$ denote the expectation and variance-covariance operators with respect to ${\mathbb P}_n$ on $\{0,1\}^n$. Define $s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta) := \partial \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)/\partial\beta$ and note that by assumption $\beta\mapsto s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)$ is continuously differentiable on ${\mathbb R}^{m(\mathbb M)}$, for all $y\in\{0,1\}^n$. Therefore, we can expand $s_{\mathbb M,n}$ around $\beta_0\in{\mathbb R}^{m(\mathbb M)}$ as follows, \begin{align*} s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta) - s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_0) =\; \int\limits_0^1 H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,t\beta + (1-t) \beta_0) dt\cdot (\beta_0-\beta). \end{align*} For $n$ sufficiently large, such that $\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^* = \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*({\mathbb P}_n)$ of Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudo} exists, define $\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) := \int_0^1 H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,t\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^* + (1-t)\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y))\,dt$ and note that with this we have \begin{equation} s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) \;:=\; s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) \;=\; \tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)\cdot(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*), \end{equation} for $y\in E_{\mathbb M,n} := E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}$, the set defined in Lemma~\ref{lemma:unifCons}. Moreover, since $H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)$ is positive definite under Conditions~\ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:C2}) and \ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:rank}, so are $\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)$ and $H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) := H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)$. Thus, if we set $$ \psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) \;:=\; y_i\dot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) + (1-y_i)\dot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*), $$ $$ g_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y_i) \;:=\; {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} X_{i,n}[M]' \left( \psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - {\mathbb E}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*] \right), $$ and $$ \Delta_{n,\mathbb M}(y) \;:=\; \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^* - \sum_{i=1}^n g_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y_i), $$ we see that \eqref{eq:repres} is satisfied, that ${\mathbb E}_n[g_{i,n,\mathbb M}] = 0$, $r_{n,\mathbb M}(y) := \sum_{i=1}^n g_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y_i) = {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)$, because ${\mathbb E}_n[s_{\mathbb M,n}^*] = 0$, and that ${\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]$ is given by \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^n \left(e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\right)^2 {\mathbb V}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*], \end{align*} where $e_m(j)$ is the $j$-th element of the canonical basis in ${\mathbb R}^m$ and $j\in\{1,\dots, m(\mathbb M)\}$. Note that by Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudoBound}, Conditions~\ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:cdf},\ref{cH:C2},\ref{cH:Hdot}) and the finiteness of $\mathcal H$, there exists a positive constant $\underline{K'}(\tau, C)$, depending only on $\tau>0$ and $C$ from Condition~\ref{cond:X2}, such that for all large $n$, \begin{align*} \infty > {\mathbb V}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*] &\ge \tau \left(\frac{\dot{h}(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)}{h(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)} + \frac{\dot{h}(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)}{1-h(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)}\right)^2\\ &\ge \underline{K'}(\tau, C) > 0. \end{align*} In particular, for such $n$, we have $0 < {\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}] < \infty$. Furthermore, by a similar argument, we obtain the upper bound $|\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i)|^2\le \overline{K'}(\tau, C)$ and, in turn, \begin{align} \frac{|g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i)|^2}{{\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]} \le 2\frac{\overline{K'}(\tau, C)}{\underline{K'}(\tau, C)} \frac{ \left( e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\right)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n \left(e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\right)^2}. \end{align} But the numerator of the second fraction on the right of the previous display can be bounded by \begin{align*} &\|(X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{1/2}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2 \|(X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{-1/2}X_{i,n}[M]'\|^2\\ &\quad\le \|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2 \cdot C/n, \end{align*} in view of Condition~\ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:Huber}, whereas the denominator of that same fraction coincides with $\|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2$. Thus, we conclude that also \eqref{eq:linde} is satisfied. Finally, for asymptotic negligibility of ${\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]^{-1/2}\Delta_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y)$, first note that using \eqref{eq:thm:binary:sstar}, for $y\in E_{\mathbb M,n}$, we have \begin{align*} &\Delta_{n,\mathbb M}(y) = \tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) \\ &= \left(\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*] - I_{m(\mathbb M)} \right){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)\\ &= {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}\left({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)} \right) {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\\ &\quad\times R_{n,\mathbb M}^{1/2} R_{n,\mathbb M}^{-1/2}r_{n,\mathbb M}(y), \end{align*} where $R_{n,\mathbb M} = \mathrm{diag}({\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(1)}], \dots, {\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(m(\mathbb M))}])$. Therefore, \begin{align*} &\|R_{n,\mathbb M}^{-1/2}\Delta_{n,\mathbb M}(y)\| \\ &\quad\le \|{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| \frac{\lambda_{\max}({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2})}{\lambda_{\min}({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2})}\\ &\quad\quad\times\frac{\max_j {\mathbb V}_n^{1/2}[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]}{\min_j {\mathbb V}_n^{1/2}[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]} \|R_{n,\mathbb M}^{-1/2}r_{n,\mathbb M}(y)\|. \end{align*} Here, $R_{n,\mathbb M}^{-1/2}r_{n,\mathbb M}(y)$ has mean zero and covariance matrix with ones on the main diagonal, and consequently its norm is bounded in probability. The ratio of the largest and smallest variance component of $r_{n,\mathbb M}$ is bounded by the condition number of the matrix ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_n[M]'X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}$ times a constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$, because of the previously derived upper and lower bounds on $|\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i)|^2$ and ${\mathbb V}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*]$, respectively. But this condition number is eventually bounded by a finite constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$ from Condition~\ref{cond:X2}, in view of Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:C}. In particular, this lemma shows that the condition number of ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]$ is bounded, eventually. Therefore, since ${\mathbb P}_n(E_{\mathbb M,n})\to 1$, as $n\to\infty$, it remains to show that ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2} \to I_{m(\mathbb M)}$, in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability. The result follows if we can show that the eigenvalues of $H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}$ and of ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}$ converge to $1$, in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability, because for $A={\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]$, $B=\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)$ and $C=H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)$, we have \begin{align*} &\| A^{1/2}B^{-1}A^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| \\ &= \| A^{1/2}C^{-1/2}C^{1/2}B^{-1}C^{1/2}C^{-1/2}A^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| \\ &\le \| A^{1/2}C^{-1}A^{1/2}\| \|C^{1/2}B^{-1}C^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| + \|A^{1/2}C^{-1}A^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|. \end{align*} For the first of these two, let $N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta) := N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:B}, which is a convex set, and note that for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every $\delta>0$, \begin{align*} &{\mathbb P}_n\left( \|H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|>\varepsilon\right)\\ &\quad\le {\mathbb P}_n\Big( \sup_{\beta\in N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)}\|H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|>\varepsilon,\\ &\hspace{2cm} \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}\in N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)\Big) + {\mathbb P}_n\left( \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}\notin N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)\right)\\ &\quad= o(1) + {\mathbb P}_n\left( \sqrt{n}\|U_{M,n}^{1/2}(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n} - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)\|>\delta\right), \end{align*} where $U_{M,n} = X_n[M]'X_n[M]/n$. Since $\delta>0$ was arbitrary Lemma~\ref{lemma:unifCons} shows that the probability on the far left-hand-side of the previous display converges to zero as $n\to\infty$. Finally, for $v_1, v_2\in{\mathbb R}^{m(\mathbb M)}$ with $\|v_1\|=\|v_2\|=1$, write \begin{align*} &v_1'({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)})v_2\\ &= \sum_{i=1}^n v_1'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}X_{i,n}[M]'X_{i,n}[M] {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}v_2 \\ &\hspace{2cm} \times \left(D_{i,\mathbb M,n}^*(y_i) - {\mathbb E}_n[D_{i,\mathbb M,n}^*] \right), \end{align*} where $D_{i,\mathbb M,n}^*(y_i) = -y_i\ddot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) - (1-y_i)\ddot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)$ and \linebreak ${\mathbb V}_n[D_{i,\mathbb M,n}^*]$ is bounded by a constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$. The mean of the expression in the previous display is clearly equal to zero, while its variance is bounded by $\sum_{i=1}^n (X_{i,n}[M] {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]')^2$ times a constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$. In view of Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:A} and Condition~\ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:Huber}, the latter sum is itself bounded by $$\sum_{i=1}^n (X_{i,n}[M] (X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]')^2 \le n C^2 /n^2 \to 0,$$ where we have omitted another constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$. We have thus verified Condition~\ref{cond:sum}. To show that the proposed estimators $\hat{\sigma}_{j,\mathbb M,n}^2$ of \eqref{eq:Sbinary} consistently overestimate the asymptotic variances of the MLE, we verify the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{prop:overest} with $$ \tilde{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) = \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y), $$ and $a_{i,n,\mathbb M} = {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'{\mathbb E}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*]$, where $\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) = H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y))$ and $\hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) = y_i\dot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M]\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)) + (1-y_i)\dot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M]\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y))$. In particular, $\hat{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) = \tilde{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) - a_{i,n,\mathbb M}$. First note that for any $\gamma\in{\mathbb R}$, $$ y_i \dot{\phi}_1(\gamma) + (1-y_i)\dot{\phi}_2(\gamma) = \frac{\dot{h}(\gamma)}{h(\gamma)(1-h(\gamma))}(y_i-h(\gamma)), $$ so that $\hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) = \hat{u}_{i,\mathbb M}(y)$ and the diagonal entries of $\tilde{S}_{\mathbb M,n}$ can, indeed, be represented as $$ \hat{\sigma}_{j,\mathbb M,n}^2(y) = \sum_{i=1}^n\left[ \tilde{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y)\right]^2, $$ for $j=1, \dots, m(\mathbb M)$, as required for the application of Proposition~\ref{prop:overest}. Next, consider \begin{align*} |g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i) - &\hat{g}^{(j)}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y)|^2 = |e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'\Big({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} X_{i,n}[M]' \psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) \\ &\quad- \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y)\Big)|^2\\ &\le 2|e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} - \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1})X_{i,n}[M]' \psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i)|^2\\ &\quad+ 2|e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]' (\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - \hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y))|^2\\ &\le 2|e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} - \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1})X_{i,n}[M]'|^2 \overline{K'}(\tau, C)\\ &\quad+ 2|e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]' (\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - \hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y))|^2. \end{align*} We want to show that $$ \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \left[ g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i) - \hat{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y) \right]^2}{{\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]} \le \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \left[ g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i) - \hat{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y) \right]^2}{\underline{K'}(\tau,C) \|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2}, $$ converges to zero in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability, as in \eqref{eq:negldiff2}, where the inequality follows by the same argument as in \eqref{eq:thm:binary:bound}. Hence, it suffices to show that \begin{equation} \frac{\|X_n[M]({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} - \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1})e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2 }{\|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \frac{\|X_n[M]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2}{\|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2}\max_{i=1,\dots, n} (\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - \hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y))^2, \end{equation} both converge to zero in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability. For \eqref{eq:thm:binary:conv1}, simply note that this expression is bounded by $$ \|I_{m(\mathbb M)} - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}\|^2 $$ times the condition number of the matrix ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_n[M]'X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}$. We have already seen above that the latter is bounded by a constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$. To see that ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}$ converges to $I_{m(\mathbb M)}$ in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability, note that \begin{align*} &\|I_{m(\mathbb M)} - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}\|^2\\ &\quad\le \|I_{m(\mathbb M)} - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\|^2 \frac{\lambda_{\max}({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*])}{\lambda_{\min}({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*])}\\ &\quad\le \|I_{m(\mathbb M)} - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\|^2 K(\tau, C), \end{align*} by Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:C}. Furthermore, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and $\delta>0$, \begin{align*} &{\mathbb P}_n\left( \|{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|>\varepsilon\right)\\ &\quad\le {\mathbb P}_n\Big( \sup_{\beta\in N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)}\|{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|>\varepsilon\Big)\\ &\hspace{1cm} +{\mathbb P}_n\Big(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n} \notin N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)\Big), \end{align*} and we have already seen before that this entails convergence to zero of the probability on the left-hand-side of the previous display. We conclude that \eqref{eq:thm:binary:conv1} does converge to zero in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability. To establish the same convergence also for \eqref{eq:thm:binary:conv2}, first note that it follows from the previous arguments that the fraction in that display is bounded in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability. Finally, we have to establish the desired convergence for the maximum in that display. But this follows from the continuity of $\dot{\phi}_1$ and $\dot{\phi}_2$ on ${\mathbb R}$, the bound on $|X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*|$ from Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudoBound} and the consistency of Lemma~\ref{lemma:unifCons}. Therefore, Proposition~\ref{prop:overest} shows that \eqref{eqn:special2} is satisfied. Note that ${\mathbb{V}}_n(r_n)$ has rank no larger than $\min(k,n)$, where $r_n = (r_{n,\mathbb M})_{\mathbb M\in\mathsf{M}_n}$. Hence, Theorem~\ref{thm:cons}, together with Lemma~\ref{lem:upper}, finishes the proof.\hfill\qed
nodes.statement_short: Linearize the score to verify Condition 1, then verify Proposition 2.7 for the sandwich estimator, and conclude with Theorem 2.6 and Lemma 2.9.

nodes.name: Verify Condition 1
nodes.statement: Fix $n\in{\mathbb N}$, a candidate model $\mathbb M\in\mathsf{M}_n$ and ${\mathbb P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)$, and let ${\mathbb E}_n$ and ${\mathbb V}_n$ denote the expectation and variance-covariance operators with respect to ${\mathbb P}_n$ on $\{0,1\}^n$. Define $s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta) := \partial \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)/\partial\beta$ and note that by assumption $\beta\mapsto s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)$ is continuously differentiable on ${\mathbb R}^{m(\mathbb M)}$, for all $y\in\{0,1\}^n$. Therefore, we can expand $s_{\mathbb M,n}$ around $\beta_0\in{\mathbb R}^{m(\mathbb M)}$ as follows, \begin{align*} s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta) - s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_0) =\; \int\limits_0^1 H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,t\beta + (1-t) \beta_0) dt\cdot (\beta_0-\beta). \end{align*} For $n$ sufficiently large, such that $\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^* = \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*({\mathbb P}_n)$ of Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudo} exists, define $\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) := \int_0^1 H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,t\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^* + (1-t)\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y))\,dt$ and note that with this we have \begin{equation} s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) \;:=\; s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) \;=\; \tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)\cdot(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*), \end{equation} for $y\in E_{\mathbb M,n} := E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}$, the set defined in Lemma~\ref{lemma:unifCons}. Moreover, since $H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)$ is positive definite under Conditions~\ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:C2}) and \ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:rank}, so are $\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)$ and $H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) := H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)$. Thus, if we set $$ \psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) \;:=\; y_i\dot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) + (1-y_i)\dot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*), $$ $$ g_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y_i) \;:=\; {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} X_{i,n}[M]' \left( \psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - {\mathbb E}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*] \right), $$ and $$ \Delta_{n,\mathbb M}(y) \;:=\; \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^* - \sum_{i=1}^n g_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y_i), $$ we see that \eqref{eq:repres} is satisfied, that ${\mathbb E}_n[g_{i,n,\mathbb M}] = 0$, $r_{n,\mathbb M}(y) := \sum_{i=1}^n g_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y_i) = {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)$, because ${\mathbb E}_n[s_{\mathbb M,n}^*] = 0$, and that ${\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]$ is given by \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^n \left(e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\right)^2 {\mathbb V}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*], \end{align*} where $e_m(j)$ is the $j$-th element of the canonical basis in ${\mathbb R}^m$ and $j\in\{1,\dots, m(\mathbb M)\}$. Note that by Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudoBound}, Conditions~\ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:cdf},\ref{cH:C2},\ref{cH:Hdot}) and the finiteness of $\mathcal H$, there exists a positive constant $\underline{K'}(\tau, C)$, depending only on $\tau>0$ and $C$ from Condition~\ref{cond:X2}, such that for all large $n$, \begin{align*} \infty > {\mathbb V}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*] &\ge \tau \left(\frac{\dot{h}(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)}{h(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)} + \frac{\dot{h}(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)}{1-h(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)}\right)^2\\ &\ge \underline{K'}(\tau, C) > 0. \end{align*} In particular, for such $n$, we have $0 < {\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}] < \infty$. Furthermore, by a similar argument, we obtain the upper bound $|\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i)|^2\le \overline{K'}(\tau, C)$ and, in turn, \begin{align} \frac{|g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i)|^2}{{\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]} \le 2\frac{\overline{K'}(\tau, C)}{\underline{K'}(\tau, C)} \frac{ \left( e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\right)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n \left(e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\right)^2}. \end{align} But the numerator of the second fraction on the right of the previous display can be bounded by \begin{align*} &\|(X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{1/2}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2 \|(X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{-1/2}X_{i,n}[M]'\|^2\\ &\quad\le \|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2 \cdot C/n, \end{align*} in view of Condition~\ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:Huber}, whereas the denominator of that same fraction coincides with $\|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2$. Thus, we conclude that also \eqref{eq:linde} is satisfied. Finally, for asymptotic negligibility of ${\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]^{-1/2}\Delta_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y)$, first note that using \eqref{eq:thm:binary:sstar}, for $y\in E_{\mathbb M,n}$, we have \begin{align*} &\Delta_{n,\mathbb M}(y) = \tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) \\ &= \left(\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*] - I_{m(\mathbb M)} \right){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)\\ &= {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}\left({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)} \right) {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\\ &\quad\times R_{n,\mathbb M}^{1/2} R_{n,\mathbb M}^{-1/2}r_{n,\mathbb M}(y), \end{align*} where $R_{n,\mathbb M} = \mathrm{diag}({\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(1)}], \dots, {\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(m(\mathbb M))}])$. Therefore, \begin{align*} &\|R_{n,\mathbb M}^{-1/2}\Delta_{n,\mathbb M}(y)\| \\ &\quad\le \|{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| \frac{\lambda_{\max}({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2})}{\lambda_{\min}({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2})}\\ &\quad\quad\times\frac{\max_j {\mathbb V}_n^{1/2}[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]}{\min_j {\mathbb V}_n^{1/2}[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]} \|R_{n,\mathbb M}^{-1/2}r_{n,\mathbb M}(y)\|. \end{align*} Here, $R_{n,\mathbb M}^{-1/2}r_{n,\mathbb M}(y)$ has mean zero and covariance matrix with ones on the main diagonal, and consequently its norm is bounded in probability. The ratio of the largest and smallest variance component of $r_{n,\mathbb M}$ is bounded by the condition number of the matrix ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_n[M]'X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}$ times a constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$, because of the previously derived upper and lower bounds on $|\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i)|^2$ and ${\mathbb V}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*]$, respectively. But this condition number is eventually bounded by a finite constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$ from Condition~\ref{cond:X2}, in view of Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:C}. In particular, this lemma shows that the condition number of ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]$ is bounded, eventually. Therefore, since ${\mathbb P}_n(E_{\mathbb M,n})\to 1$, as $n\to\infty$, it remains to show that ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2} \to I_{m(\mathbb M)}$, in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability. The result follows if we can show that the eigenvalues of $H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}$ and of ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}$ converge to $1$, in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability, because for $A={\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]$, $B=\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)$ and $C=H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)$, we have \begin{align*} &\| A^{1/2}B^{-1}A^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| \\ &= \| A^{1/2}C^{-1/2}C^{1/2}B^{-1}C^{1/2}C^{-1/2}A^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| \\ &\le \| A^{1/2}C^{-1}A^{1/2}\| \|C^{1/2}B^{-1}C^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| + \|A^{1/2}C^{-1}A^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|. \end{align*} For the first of these two, let $N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta) := N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:B}, which is a convex set, and note that for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every $\delta>0$, \begin{align*} &{\mathbb P}_n\left( \|H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|>\varepsilon\right)\\ &\quad\le {\mathbb P}_n\Big( \sup_{\beta\in N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)}\|H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|>\varepsilon,\\ &\hspace{2cm} \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}\in N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)\Big) + {\mathbb P}_n\left( \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}\notin N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)\right)\\ &\quad= o(1) + {\mathbb P}_n\left( \sqrt{n}\|U_{M,n}^{1/2}(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n} - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)\|>\delta\right), \end{align*} where $U_{M,n} = X_n[M]'X_n[M]/n$. Since $\delta>0$ was arbitrary Lemma~\ref{lemma:unifCons} shows that the probability on the far left-hand-side of the previous display converges to zero as $n\to\infty$. Finally, for $v_1, v_2\in{\mathbb R}^{m(\mathbb M)}$ with $\|v_1\|=\|v_2\|=1$, write \begin{align*} &v_1'({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)})v_2\\ &= \sum_{i=1}^n v_1'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}X_{i,n}[M]'X_{i,n}[M] {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}v_2 \\ &\hspace{2cm} \times \left(D_{i,\mathbb M,n}^*(y_i) - {\mathbb E}_n[D_{i,\mathbb M,n}^*] \right), \end{align*} where $D_{i,\mathbb M,n}^*(y_i) = -y_i\ddot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) - (1-y_i)\ddot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)$ and \linebreak ${\mathbb V}_n[D_{i,\mathbb M,n}^*]$ is bounded by a constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$. The mean of the expression in the previous display is clearly equal to zero, while its variance is bounded by $\sum_{i=1}^n (X_{i,n}[M] {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]')^2$ times a constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$. In view of Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:A} and Condition~\ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:Huber}, the latter sum is itself bounded by $$\sum_{i=1}^n (X_{i,n}[M] (X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]')^2 \le n C^2 /n^2 \to 0,$$ where we have omitted another constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$. We have thus verified Condition~\ref{cond:sum}.
nodes.statement_short: Verify Condition 1 for the quasi-MLE.

nodes.name: Score expansion
nodes.statement: Fix $n\in{\mathbb N}$, a candidate model $\mathbb M\in\mathsf{M}_n$ and ${\mathbb P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)$, and let ${\mathbb E}_n$ and ${\mathbb V}_n$ denote the expectation and variance-covariance operators with respect to ${\mathbb P}_n$ on $\{0,1\}^n$. Define $s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta) := \partial \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)/\partial\beta$ and note that by assumption $\beta\mapsto s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)$ is continuously differentiable on ${\mathbb R}^{m(\mathbb M)}$, for all $y\in\{0,1\}^n$. Therefore, we can expand $s_{\mathbb M,n}$ around $\beta_0\in{\mathbb R}^{m(\mathbb M)}$ as follows, \begin{align*} s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta) - s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_0) =\; \int\limits_0^1 H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,t\beta + (1-t) \beta_0) dt\cdot (\beta_0-\beta). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Mean-value expansion of the score.

nodes.name: Averaged Hessian
nodes.statement: For $n$ sufficiently large, such that $\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^* = \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*({\mathbb P}_n)$ of Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudo} exists, define $\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) := \int_0^1 H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,t\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^* + (1-t)\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y))\,dt$ and note that with this we have \begin{equation} s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) \;:=\; s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) \;=\; \tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)\cdot(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*), \end{equation} for $y\in E_{\mathbb M,n} := E_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}$, the set defined in Lemma~\ref{lemma:unifCons}. Moreover, since $H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)$ is positive definite under Conditions~\ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:C2}) and \ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:rank}, so are $\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)$ and $H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) := H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\tilde H$ so that $s^*=\tilde H(\hat\beta-\beta^*)$.

nodes.name: Equation (D.27) [eq:thm:binary:sstar]
nodes.statement: s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) \;:=\; s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) \;=\; \tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)\cdot(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*),
nodes.label: eq:thm:binary:sstar

nodes.name: Linear representation
nodes.statement: Thus, if we set $$ \psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) \;:=\; y_i\dot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) + (1-y_i)\dot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*), $$ $$ g_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y_i) \;:=\; {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} X_{i,n}[M]' \left( \psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - {\mathbb E}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*] \right), $$ and $$ \Delta_{n,\mathbb M}(y) \;:=\; \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^* - \sum_{i=1}^n g_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y_i), $$ we see that \eqref{eq:repres} is satisfied, that ${\mathbb E}_n[g_{i,n,\mathbb M}] = 0$, $r_{n,\mathbb M}(y) := \sum_{i=1}^n g_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y_i) = {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)$, because ${\mathbb E}_n[s_{\mathbb M,n}^*] = 0$, and that ${\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]$ is given by \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^n \left(e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\right)^2 {\mathbb V}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*], \end{align*} where $e_m(j)$ is the $j$-th element of the canonical basis in ${\mathbb R}^m$ and $j\in\{1,\dots, m(\mathbb M)\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\psi^*$, $g$ and $\Delta$ giving representation (2.1).

nodes.name: Variance lower bound
nodes.statement: Note that by Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudoBound}, Conditions~\ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:cdf},\ref{cH:C2},\ref{cH:Hdot}) and the finiteness of $\mathcal H$, there exists a positive constant $\underline{K'}(\tau, C)$, depending only on $\tau>0$ and $C$ from Condition~\ref{cond:X2}, such that for all large $n$, \begin{align*} \infty > {\mathbb V}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*] &\ge \tau \left(\frac{\dot{h}(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)}{h(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)} + \frac{\dot{h}(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)}{1-h(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)}\right)^2\\ &\ge \underline{K'}(\tau, C) > 0. \end{align*} In particular, for such $n$, we have $0 < {\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}] < \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Variance of $\psi^*$ bounded away from zero.

nodes.name: Lindeberg
nodes.statement: Furthermore, by a similar argument, we obtain the upper bound $|\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i)|^2\le \overline{K'}(\tau, C)$ and, in turn, \begin{align} \frac{|g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i)|^2}{{\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]} \le 2\frac{\overline{K'}(\tau, C)}{\underline{K'}(\tau, C)} \frac{ \left( e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\right)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n \left(e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\right)^2}. \end{align} But the numerator of the second fraction on the right of the previous display can be bounded by \begin{align*} &\|(X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{1/2}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2 \|(X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{-1/2}X_{i,n}[M]'\|^2\\ &\quad\le \|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2 \cdot C/n, \end{align*} in view of Condition~\ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:Huber}, whereas the denominator of that same fraction coincides with $\|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2$. Thus, we conclude that also \eqref{eq:linde} is satisfied.
nodes.statement_short: Lindeberg condition via the leverage bound.

nodes.name: Equation (D.28) [eq:thm:binary:bound]
nodes.statement: \frac{|g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i)|^2}{{\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]} \le 2\frac{\overline{K'}(\tau, C)}{\underline{K'}(\tau, C)} \frac{ \left( e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\right)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n \left(e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\right)^2}.
nodes.label: eq:thm:binary:bound

nodes.name: Remainder representation
nodes.statement: Finally, for asymptotic negligibility of ${\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]^{-1/2}\Delta_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y)$, first note that using \eqref{eq:thm:binary:sstar}, for $y\in E_{\mathbb M,n}$, we have \begin{align*} &\Delta_{n,\mathbb M}(y) = \tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) \\ &= \left(\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*] - I_{m(\mathbb M)} \right){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)\\ &= {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}\left({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)} \right) {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\\ &\quad\times R_{n,\mathbb M}^{1/2} R_{n,\mathbb M}^{-1/2}r_{n,\mathbb M}(y), \end{align*} where $R_{n,\mathbb M} = \mathrm{diag}({\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(1)}], \dots, {\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(m(\mathbb M))}])$. Therefore, \begin{align*} &\|R_{n,\mathbb M}^{-1/2}\Delta_{n,\mathbb M}(y)\| \\ &\quad\le \|{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| \frac{\lambda_{\max}({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2})}{\lambda_{\min}({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2})}\\ &\quad\quad\times\frac{\max_j {\mathbb V}_n^{1/2}[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]}{\min_j {\mathbb V}_n^{1/2}[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]} \|R_{n,\mathbb M}^{-1/2}r_{n,\mathbb M}(y)\|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Express the remainder $\Delta$ through $\tilde H^{-1}\mathbb{E}[H^*]$.

nodes.name: Bounded factors
nodes.statement: Here, $R_{n,\mathbb M}^{-1/2}r_{n,\mathbb M}(y)$ has mean zero and covariance matrix with ones on the main diagonal, and consequently its norm is bounded in probability. The ratio of the largest and smallest variance component of $r_{n,\mathbb M}$ is bounded by the condition number of the matrix ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_n[M]'X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}$ times a constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$, because of the previously derived upper and lower bounds on $|\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i)|^2$ and ${\mathbb V}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*]$, respectively. But this condition number is eventually bounded by a finite constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$ from Condition~\ref{cond:X2}, in view of Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:C}. In particular, this lemma shows that the condition number of ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]$ is bounded, eventually.
nodes.statement_short: Other factors bounded via Lemma D.2(iii).

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: Therefore, since ${\mathbb P}_n(E_{\mathbb M,n})\to 1$, as $n\to\infty$, it remains to show that ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2} \to I_{m(\mathbb M)}$, in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability. The result follows if we can show that the eigenvalues of $H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}$ and of ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}$ converge to $1$, in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability, because for $A={\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]$, $B=\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)$ and $C=H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)$, we have \begin{align*} &\| A^{1/2}B^{-1}A^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| \\ &= \| A^{1/2}C^{-1/2}C^{1/2}B^{-1}C^{1/2}C^{-1/2}A^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| \\ &\le \| A^{1/2}C^{-1}A^{1/2}\| \|C^{1/2}B^{-1}C^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\| + \|A^{1/2}C^{-1}A^{1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to eigenvalue convergence of two matrices.

nodes.name: First matrix
nodes.statement: For the first of these two, let $N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta) := N_{\mathbb M,{\mathbb P}_n,n}(\delta)$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:B}, which is a convex set, and note that for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every $\delta>0$, \begin{align*} &{\mathbb P}_n\left( \|H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2}\tilde{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|>\varepsilon\right)\\ &\quad\le {\mathbb P}_n\Big( \sup_{\beta\in N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)}\|H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y)^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|>\varepsilon,\\ &\hspace{2cm} \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}\in N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)\Big) + {\mathbb P}_n\left( \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}\notin N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)\right)\\ &\quad= o(1) + {\mathbb P}_n\left( \sqrt{n}\|U_{M,n}^{1/2}(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n} - \beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)\|>\delta\right), \end{align*} where $U_{M,n} = X_n[M]'X_n[M]/n$. Since $\delta>0$ was arbitrary Lemma~\ref{lemma:unifCons} shows that the probability on the far left-hand-side of the previous display converges to zero as $n\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: First matrix via Lemma D.2(ii) and Lemma 3.10.

nodes.name: Second matrix
nodes.statement: Finally, for $v_1, v_2\in{\mathbb R}^{m(\mathbb M)}$ with $\|v_1\|=\|v_2\|=1$, write \begin{align*} &v_1'({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)})v_2\\ &= \sum_{i=1}^n v_1'{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}X_{i,n}[M]'X_{i,n}[M] {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}v_2 \\ &\hspace{2cm} \times \left(D_{i,\mathbb M,n}^*(y_i) - {\mathbb E}_n[D_{i,\mathbb M,n}^*] \right), \end{align*} where $D_{i,\mathbb M,n}^*(y_i) = -y_i\ddot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*) - (1-y_i)\ddot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)$ and \linebreak ${\mathbb V}_n[D_{i,\mathbb M,n}^*]$ is bounded by a constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$. The mean of the expression in the previous display is clearly equal to zero, while its variance is bounded by $\sum_{i=1}^n (X_{i,n}[M] {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]')^2$ times a constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$. In view of Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:A} and Condition~\ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:Huber}, the latter sum is itself bounded by $$\sum_{i=1}^n (X_{i,n}[M] (X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]')^2 \le n C^2 /n^2 \to 0,$$ where we have omitted another constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$. We have thus verified Condition~\ref{cond:sum}.
nodes.statement_short: Second matrix by a variance bound; Condition 1 verified.

nodes.name: Verify overestimation
nodes.statement: To show that the proposed estimators $\hat{\sigma}_{j,\mathbb M,n}^2$ of \eqref{eq:Sbinary} consistently overestimate the asymptotic variances of the MLE, we verify the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{prop:overest} with $$ \tilde{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) = \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y), $$ and $a_{i,n,\mathbb M} = {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'{\mathbb E}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*]$, where $\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) = H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y))$ and $\hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) = y_i\dot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M]\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)) + (1-y_i)\dot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M]\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y))$. In particular, $\hat{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) = \tilde{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) - a_{i,n,\mathbb M}$. First note that for any $\gamma\in{\mathbb R}$, $$ y_i \dot{\phi}_1(\gamma) + (1-y_i)\dot{\phi}_2(\gamma) = \frac{\dot{h}(\gamma)}{h(\gamma)(1-h(\gamma))}(y_i-h(\gamma)), $$ so that $\hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) = \hat{u}_{i,\mathbb M}(y)$ and the diagonal entries of $\tilde{S}_{\mathbb M,n}$ can, indeed, be represented as $$ \hat{\sigma}_{j,\mathbb M,n}^2(y) = \sum_{i=1}^n\left[ \tilde{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y)\right]^2, $$ for $j=1, \dots, m(\mathbb M)$, as required for the application of Proposition~\ref{prop:overest}. Next, consider \begin{align*} |g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i) - &\hat{g}^{(j)}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y)|^2 = |e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'\Big({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} X_{i,n}[M]' \psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) \\ &\quad- \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y)\Big)|^2\\ &\le 2|e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} - \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1})X_{i,n}[M]' \psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i)|^2\\ &\quad+ 2|e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]' (\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - \hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y))|^2\\ &\le 2|e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} - \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1})X_{i,n}[M]'|^2 \overline{K'}(\tau, C)\\ &\quad+ 2|e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]' (\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - \hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y))|^2. \end{align*} We want to show that $$ \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \left[ g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i) - \hat{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y) \right]^2}{{\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]} \le \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \left[ g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i) - \hat{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y) \right]^2}{\underline{K'}(\tau,C) \|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2}, $$ converges to zero in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability, as in \eqref{eq:negldiff2}, where the inequality follows by the same argument as in \eqref{eq:thm:binary:bound}. Hence, it suffices to show that \begin{equation} \frac{\|X_n[M]({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} - \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1})e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2 }{\|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \frac{\|X_n[M]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2}{\|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2}\max_{i=1,\dots, n} (\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - \hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y))^2, \end{equation} both converge to zero in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability. For \eqref{eq:thm:binary:conv1}, simply note that this expression is bounded by $$ \|I_{m(\mathbb M)} - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}\|^2 $$ times the condition number of the matrix ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_n[M]'X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}$. We have already seen above that the latter is bounded by a constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$. To see that ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}$ converges to $I_{m(\mathbb M)}$ in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability, note that \begin{align*} &\|I_{m(\mathbb M)} - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}\|^2\\ &\quad\le \|I_{m(\mathbb M)} - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\|^2 \frac{\lambda_{\max}({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*])}{\lambda_{\min}({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*])}\\ &\quad\le \|I_{m(\mathbb M)} - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\|^2 K(\tau, C), \end{align*} by Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:C}. Furthermore, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and $\delta>0$, \begin{align*} &{\mathbb P}_n\left( \|{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|>\varepsilon\right)\\ &\quad\le {\mathbb P}_n\Big( \sup_{\beta\in N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)}\|{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|>\varepsilon\Big)\\ &\hspace{1cm} +{\mathbb P}_n\Big(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n} \notin N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)\Big), \end{align*} and we have already seen before that this entails convergence to zero of the probability on the left-hand-side of the previous display. We conclude that \eqref{eq:thm:binary:conv1} does converge to zero in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability. To establish the same convergence also for \eqref{eq:thm:binary:conv2}, first note that it follows from the previous arguments that the fraction in that display is bounded in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability. Finally, we have to establish the desired convergence for the maximum in that display. But this follows from the continuity of $\dot{\phi}_1$ and $\dot{\phi}_2$ on ${\mathbb R}$, the bound on $|X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*|$ from Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudoBound} and the consistency of Lemma~\ref{lemma:unifCons}.
nodes.statement_short: Verify the assumptions of Proposition 2.7 for the sandwich estimator.

nodes.name: Predictors
nodes.statement: To show that the proposed estimators $\hat{\sigma}_{j,\mathbb M,n}^2$ of \eqref{eq:Sbinary} consistently overestimate the asymptotic variances of the MLE, we verify the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{prop:overest} with $$ \tilde{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) = \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y), $$ and $a_{i,n,\mathbb M} = {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'{\mathbb E}_n[\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*]$, where $\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y) = H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y))$ and $\hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) = y_i\dot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M]\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)) + (1-y_i)\dot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M]\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n}(y))$. In particular, $\hat{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) = \tilde{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) - a_{i,n,\mathbb M}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\tilde g$ and $a$.

nodes.name: Identification
nodes.statement: First note that for any $\gamma\in{\mathbb R}$, $$ y_i \dot{\phi}_1(\gamma) + (1-y_i)\dot{\phi}_2(\gamma) = \frac{\dot{h}(\gamma)}{h(\gamma)(1-h(\gamma))}(y_i-h(\gamma)), $$ so that $\hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y) = \hat{u}_{i,\mathbb M}(y)$ and the diagonal entries of $\tilde{S}_{\mathbb M,n}$ can, indeed, be represented as $$ \hat{\sigma}_{j,\mathbb M,n}^2(y) = \sum_{i=1}^n\left[ \tilde{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y)\right]^2, $$ for $j=1, \dots, m(\mathbb M)$, as required for the application of Proposition~\ref{prop:overest}.
nodes.statement_short: Identify $\hat\psi=\hat u$ and the diagonal of $\tilde S$.

nodes.name: Error bound
nodes.statement: Next, consider \begin{align*} |g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i) - &\hat{g}^{(j)}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y)|^2 = |e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'\Big({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} X_{i,n}[M]' \psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) \\ &\quad- \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]'\hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y)\Big)|^2\\ &\le 2|e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} - \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1})X_{i,n}[M]' \psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i)|^2\\ &\quad+ 2|e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]' (\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - \hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y))|^2\\ &\le 2|e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} - \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1})X_{i,n}[M]'|^2 \overline{K'}(\tau, C)\\ &\quad+ 2|e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)'\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}X_{i,n}[M]' (\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - \hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y))|^2. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $|g-\hat g|^2$ by two terms.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: We want to show that $$ \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \left[ g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i) - \hat{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y) \right]^2}{{\mathbb V}_n[r_{n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}]} \le \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \left[ g_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y_i) - \hat{g}_{i,n,\mathbb M}^{(j)}(y) \right]^2}{\underline{K'}(\tau,C) \|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2}, $$ converges to zero in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability, as in \eqref{eq:negldiff2}, where the inequality follows by the same argument as in \eqref{eq:thm:binary:bound}. Hence, it suffices to show that \begin{equation} \frac{\|X_n[M]({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} - \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1})e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2 }{\|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \frac{\|X_n[M]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2}{\|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2}\max_{i=1,\dots, n} (\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - \hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y))^2, \end{equation} both converge to zero in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to two ratios converging to zero.

nodes.name: Equation (D.29) [eq:thm:binary:conv1]
nodes.statement: \frac{\|X_n[M]({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} - \hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1})e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j)\|^2 }{\|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2}
nodes.label: eq:thm:binary:conv1

nodes.name: Equation (D.30) [eq:thm:binary:conv2]
nodes.statement: \frac{\|X_n[M]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2}{\|X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}e_{m(\mathbb M)}(j) \|^2}\max_{i=1,\dots, n} (\psi_{i,n,\mathbb M}^*(y_i) - \hat{\psi}_{i,n,\mathbb M}(y))^2,
nodes.label: eq:thm:binary:conv2

nodes.name: First ratio
nodes.statement: For \eqref{eq:thm:binary:conv1}, simply note that this expression is bounded by $$ \|I_{m(\mathbb M)} - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}\|^2 $$ times the condition number of the matrix ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}X_n[M]'X_n[M]{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1}$. We have already seen above that the latter is bounded by a constant that depends only on $\tau$ and $C$. To see that ${\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}$ converges to $I_{m(\mathbb M)}$ in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability, note that \begin{align*} &\|I_{m(\mathbb M)} - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}\|^2\\ &\quad\le \|I_{m(\mathbb M)} - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\|^2 \frac{\lambda_{\max}({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*])}{\lambda_{\min}({\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*])}\\ &\quad\le \|I_{m(\mathbb M)} - {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y)^{-1}{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{1/2}\|^2 K(\tau, C), \end{align*} by Lemma~\ref{lemma:Hcontinuity}\ref{l:Hcont:C}. Furthermore, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and $\delta>0$, \begin{align*} &{\mathbb P}_n\left( \|{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}\hat{H}_{\mathbb M,n}(y){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|>\varepsilon\right)\\ &\quad\le {\mathbb P}_n\Big( \sup_{\beta\in N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)}\|{\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2}H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta){\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1/2} - I_{m(\mathbb M)}\|>\varepsilon\Big)\\ &\hspace{1cm} +{\mathbb P}_n\Big(\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb M,n} \notin N_{\mathbb M,n}(\delta)\Big), \end{align*} and we have already seen before that this entails convergence to zero of the probability on the left-hand-side of the previous display. We conclude that \eqref{eq:thm:binary:conv1} does converge to zero in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability.
nodes.statement_short: First ratio via Hessian consistency and Lemma D.2(iii).

nodes.name: Second ratio
nodes.statement: To establish the same convergence also for \eqref{eq:thm:binary:conv2}, first note that it follows from the previous arguments that the fraction in that display is bounded in ${\mathbb P}_n$-probability. Finally, we have to establish the desired convergence for the maximum in that display. But this follows from the continuity of $\dot{\phi}_1$ and $\dot{\phi}_2$ on ${\mathbb R}$, the bound on $|X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*|$ from Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudoBound} and the consistency of Lemma~\ref{lemma:unifCons}.
nodes.statement_short: Second ratio via continuity and Lemma 3.10.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Therefore, Proposition~\ref{prop:overest} shows that \eqref{eqn:special2} is satisfied. Note that ${\mathbb{V}}_n(r_n)$ has rank no larger than $\min(k,n)$, where $r_n = (r_{n,\mathbb M})_{\mathbb M\in\mathsf{M}_n}$. Hence, Theorem~\ref{thm:cons}, together with Lemma~\ref{lem:upper}, finishes the proof.\hfill\qed
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 2.6 with Lemma 2.9 (rank at most $\min(k,n)$).

nodes.name: Smaller POSI constant for the canonical link
nodes.statement: In the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:binary}, if $\mathcal H$ contains only the canonical link function $h^{(c)}(\gamma) = e^\gamma/(1+e^\gamma)$, then the confidence intervals \begin{equation} \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}^{(j), \mathrm{binC}} = \hat{\beta}^{(j)}_{\mathbb{M}, n} \pm \sqrt{\hat{\sigma}^2_{j,\mathbb{M}, n}} B_{\alpha}(\min(k, p),k), \end{equation} satisfy \begin{equation} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \inf_{\mathbb{P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})} \left(\tau \right) } \mathbb{P}_n \left(\beta_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n}^{*, (j)} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n}^{(j), \mathrm{binC}} \;\forall j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n) \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation}
assumptions: if $\mathcal H$ contains only the canonical link function $h^{(c)}(\gamma) = e^\gamma/(1+e^\gamma)$
nodes.label: corr:binaryCanoncial

nodes.name: Equation (D.31)
nodes.statement: \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}^{(j), \mathrm{binC}} = \hat{\beta}^{(j)}_{\mathbb{M}, n} \pm \sqrt{\hat{\sigma}^2_{j,\mathbb{M}, n}} B_{\alpha}(\min(k, p),k),

nodes.name: Equation (D.32)
nodes.statement: \liminf_{n \to \infty} \inf_{\mathbb{P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})} \left(\tau \right) } \mathbb{P}_n \left(\beta_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n}^{*, (j)} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n}^{(j), \mathrm{binC}} \;\forall j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n) \right) \geq 1-\alpha.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary D.3
nodes.statement: From the first few lines of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:binary}, we see that the $m(\mathbb M)$-dimensional sub-vector $r_{n,\mathbb M}(y)$ of $r_n(y)$ that corresponds to the model $\mathbb M\triangleq (h,M)\in\{h^{(c)}\}\times \mathcal I$, is given by $$ r_{n,\mathbb M}(y) = {\mathbb E}_n[H_{\mathbb M,n}^*]^{-1} s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y), $$ where $H_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) := H_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)$, $s_{\mathbb M,n}^*(y) := s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta_{\mathbb M,n}^*)$ and $s_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta) := \partial \ell_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)/\partial \beta = X_n[M]'C_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)$, where $C_{\mathbb M,n}(y,\beta)$ is an $n\times 1$ vector with $i$-th entry given by $y_i\dot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M]\beta) + (1-y_i)\dot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M]\beta)$. But it is easy to see that for $h=h^{(c)}$, $\phi_1(\gamma) - \phi_2(\gamma) = \gamma$ and thus $\dot{\phi}_1(\gamma) - \dot{\phi}_2(\gamma) = 1$, so that in this case the matrix ${\mathbb{V}}_n(r_n)$ reduces to $$ {\mathbb{V}}_n(r_n) = \left({\mathbb E}_n[H^*_{\mathbb M_s,n}]^{-1} X_n[M_s]'{\mathbb{V}}(Y_n)X_n[M_t]{\mathbb E}_n[H^*_{\mathbb M_t,n}]^{-1}\right)_{s,t=1}^d. $$ The rank of this matrix is not larger than $\min(k,p)$, so by Lemma~\ref{lem:upper} we obtain the smaller bound $K_{1-\alpha}(\mathrm{corr}({\mathbb{V}}_n(r_n)))\le B_\alpha(\min(k,p),k)$.
nodes.statement_short: For the logit link $\dot\phi_1-\dot\phi_2=1$, so $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$ has rank at most $\min(k,p)$; apply Lemma 2.9.
